name.description: Optional session name, surfaced to coding agents via the MCP/control plane. Falls back to the working directory name.

metadata.description: Fetch best-effort Git branch and GitHub PR metadata for session listings. Overrides the user config. Changes require restarting the session.

pretty_json_logs.description: Render structured JSON service logs as compact colored log lines in the TUI.

mouse.description: Capture the mouse in the TUI for clicks, scrolling and in-pane text selection. Overrides the user config; the --mouse flag overrides both.

copy_on_select.description: Copy a mouse selection to the clipboard as soon as the drag ends, instead of on y or Enter. Off by default. Overrides the user config; the --copy-on-select flag overrides both.

enabled.description: Enable the local control endpoint. Changes require a session restart.

dynamic_services.description: Runtime-created service policy. This is blast-radius hygiene for same-user commands, not a security sandbox. Changes require a session restart.

enabled.description: Permit runtime-created services through the local control plane.

allowed_working_roots.description: Working-directory roots, resolved and canonicalized relative to the config directory.

max_lifetime.description: Maximum and default dynamic-service lifetime. Set to 'none' to permit session-lifetime leases.

restart.description: Default restart policy inherited by services that do not set restart.

session.description: Session identity used for hostnames and the MICROMUX_SESSION variables. Changes require a session restart.

name.description: Session name, a lowercase hostname label. Defaults to the config directory's name, slugified to [a-z0-9-].

domain.description: Parent domain of the session's hostnames.

port_range.description: Inclusive range allocate_ports draws from. Defaults to 20000-32767. Pick a range no other tool on the machine allocates from, such as a testcontainers harness.

allocate_ports.description: Environment variables that each receive a free TCP port, stable across restarts of this session and never shared with another live session. An entry is a variable name, or { name, prefer } to take a well-known port whenever it is available. The values override env_file and environment definitions of the same names. Changes require a session restart.

routes.description: Hostnames, optionally narrowed to path prefixes, served by the shared micromux proxy while the session runs, as http://<host>.<session>.<domain><path>. The host decides first: a hostname any route names is served by its own routes alone, every other hostname by the catch-all's. Among those, the route with the longest prefix of the request path wins, then the route without a path; otherwise the proxy answers 404. Not supported on Windows. Changes require a session restart.

host.description: Hostname labels below the session domain, such as app or email.internal, or * for every other hostname under the session domain. A host may be listed several times with different paths.

path.description: Path prefix this route serves, such as /rest/. It matches the request path as plain, case-sensitive text without decoding, so /rest/ matches /rest/x but not /rest. Without path, the route serves every path of its host that no path route matches.

strip_prefix.description: Removes path from the request path before forwarding, so the upstream sees /token for /auth/v1/token. The forwarded path always starts with /. Requires path.

port.description: Upstream port on 127.0.0.1. May reference micromux's own environment and the session variables, such as an allocate_ports name, but not service env files.

proxy.description: Port the shared micromux proxy serves this session's routes on. Sessions with different ports share one proxy, which listens on each. Changes require a session restart.

port.description: Port the session's routes are served on. The proxy starts listening on it if it does not yet.

fallback_port.description: Port used instead when port needs privileges or is taken. Never chosen silently otherwise.

prefer.description: Port the variable takes when no other session, running or stopped, has it assigned and nothing else listens on it, otherwise keeping its previous port or falling back to session.port_range. May lie outside the range, but not on a proxy port or another entry's preferred port.

command.description: Command to execute. Either a shell-like string or an argv-like sequence. Each argument is interpolated after splitting: ${VAR} and $VAR resolve against the service's environment, ${VAR:-default} supplies a fallback, $$VAR passes a literal $VAR through, and an unset variable is an error.

env_file_entry.description: A dotenv file to load. Its path may reference ${VAR} from the environment micromux runs in.

optional.description: Skip this entry when its path names an unset variable or no file exists at the path. A present file is always loaded in full.

env_file.description: Dotenv files to load, earlier entries first. Later files override earlier ones and `environment` overrides them all.

healthcheck_defaults.description: Default healthcheck timing inherited by services that define healthcheck.test. Does not create a healthcheck by itself.

log_limit.description: A positive integer bound, or an explicit unbounded in-memory limit.

logs_memory.description: In-memory log tail retained for the TUI and default log stream.

logs.description: Log retention and TUI presentation settings. Top-level values are defaults that each service's logs block overrides. Disk run logs retain the newest bounded segment of each retained run.

retained_runs.description: Number of bounded disk-backed service runs retained, including the current/latest run (default 5).

level.description: Least severe structured JSON log level the TUI shows initially (default all). Lines without a recognizable level, such as build output and panics, always show. Change it at runtime with L; agents always read every level.

timestamps.description: Lead structured JSON log lines with their timestamp in local time in the TUI. Toggle per service at runtime with T.

filter_fields.description: Leave out the fields that `fields` hides in the TUI. Toggle per service at runtime with F.

fields.description: How the TUI displays structured JSON log fields, keyed by field name and matched exactly against top-level keys and keys of a nested tracing-style fields object. A service's map merges into the top-level one key by key, so `show` undoes an inherited `hide`. Agents always read every field.

cleanup.description: Command run to completion after each of the service's processes exits, however it exited, in the service's environment and working directory. The service is reported stopped, and restarts, only once it finished; a failure is reported but never blocks the session.

timeout.description: How long the cleanup may run before it gets the service's stop_signal and, 5s later, SIGKILL (default 60s, maximum 1h).

kind.description: `service` (the default) runs for as long as the session; `job` runs to completion. A job completes on exit status 0 and fails on any other, never restarts unless it sets `restart: on-failure`, and cannot have a healthcheck. A dependency on a job without a condition waits for it to complete.

run.description: When a job runs: `on-start` (the default) when the session starts, or `manual` only when restarted. Applies only to `kind: job`.

disabled.description: Leave this service disabled when the micromux session starts.

working_dir.description: Working directory, relative to the config file (default: the config file's directory). May reference ${VAR} from the environment micromux itself runs in; env files are not loaded yet when paths resolve.

environment.description: Inline environment variables. Values may reference ${VAR} from the environment micromux runs in, from env files, and from earlier entries; an unset variable is an error.

ports.description: Ports the service uses (metadata; not bound by micromux). Entries may reference ${VAR} and must resolve to a number between 0 and 65535.

stop_grace_period.description: Time allowed for graceful termination before forced termination (default 10s, maximum 5m).

stop_signal.description: Signal delivered for the graceful stop request (default SIGTERM). The SIG prefix is optional and matching is case-insensitive. Ignored on Windows.
